text_sentences: ['Thus, the optimal RLHF policy $\\pi^*$ under the Bradley-Terry model satisfies the preference model:', '\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:objective}', '    p^*(y_1\\succ y_2 \\mid x)=\\frac{1}{1 + \\exp\\left(\\beta \\log \\frac{\\pi^*(y_2\\mid x)}{\\pi_\\text{ref}(y_2\\mid x)} - \\beta \\log \\frac{\\pi^*(y_1\\mid x)}{\\pi_\\text{ref}(y_1\\mid x)}\\right)}', '\\end{equation}']
question_explanation: This asks what the modeled preference reduces to when the reference assigns the same probability to both options.
inference_explanation: With equal π_ref terms, the log reference probabilities cancel, leaving a function of β[log π*(y1|x) − log π*(y2|x)]—i.e., the ratio π*(y1|x)/π*(y2|x).

text_sentences: ['We assume a parameterized model $\\pi_{\\theta}(y\\mid x)$ and minimize $\\mathbb{D}_{\\text{KL}}[\\pi_{\\theta}(y|x) \\mid \\mid \\pi^*(y\\mid x)]$ where $\\pi^*$ is the optimal policy from Eq. \\ref{eq:optimum_model} induced by the reward function $r_{\\phi}(y, x)$. With some algebra this leads to the optimization objective:', 'This is the same objective optimized in prior works', '$$    \\max_{\\pi_{\\theta}}\\mathbb{E}_{\\pi_{\\theta}(y\\mid x)}\\bigg[\\underbrace{r_{\\phi}(x, y) -\\beta\\log\\sum_{y}\\pi_\\text{ref}(y\\mid x)\\exp\\left(\\frac{1}{\\beta}r_{\\phi}(x, y)\\right)}_{f(r_{\\phi}, \\pi_\\text{ref}, \\beta)} - \\underbrace{\\beta\\log\\frac{\\pi_{\\theta}(y\\mid x)}{\\pi_\\text{ref}(y\\mid x)}}_{\\text{KL}}\\bigg] $$']
question_explanation: This asks what structural restriction on the learned policy follows when the reference puts zero mass on some actions, due to the KL term.
inference_explanation: The KL term contains log(πθ/πref). If πref(y|x)=0 but πθ(y|x)>0, the log-ratio is undefined/infinite, making the objective ill-posed. Thus, πθ must place mass only where πref does: support inclusion.
